title: 25 BEGINNER BACHATA MOVES YOU MUST KNOW!

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teachers demonstrate the moves in a continuous, non-stop sequence without verbal explanation. They rely on visual modeling to convey the steps to the viewer.

lesson_structure.note: The teachers introduce the video and the 25 moves.
The teachers perform 25 beginner bachata moves in a continuous sequence.
The teachers perform a final sequence of moves.

extraction.counting_scheme: the teachers do not use a verbal counting scheme

steps_taught.name: Two Hands' Turn
steps_taught.description: A turn performed while holding both hands.

steps_taught.name: Pretzel Turn
steps_taught.description: A complex turn involving arm entanglement.

steps_taught.name: Arm Breaker / Hammerlock
steps_taught.description: A move involving a hammerlock position.

steps_taught.name: Open-Close
steps_taught.description: A transition between open and closed positions.

steps_taught.name: Change Places
steps_taught.description: A move where partners switch sides.

what_works: The video provides a clear, continuous visual demonstration of all 25 moves.
what_hinders: The lack of verbal explanation or breakdown makes it difficult for beginners to learn the specific footwork and timing.

quotes.text: In this video, we are going to show you 25 moves in Bachata.
If you want a more detailed tutorial, check the description down below.

evidence_segments.observation: The teachers stand side-by-side, speaking directly to the camera to introduce the content.
The teachers perform a side-to-side basic step in a closed position.
The teachers perform a front basic step while holding hands.
The teachers perform a box step in a closed position.
The leader guides the follower into a turn.
The leader performs a turn while the follower remains in place.

extraction.distinctive_method: The video is a continuous, non-stop demonstration of 25 moves without any verbal instruction or breakdown, relying entirely on visual modeling.
